summary: Unlike every other entry in this document, this section is not a claim backed by citations - it is the document owner's own interpretive read of the pattern across the entries above, recorded here so it is not confused with the sourced material. The thesis: having a president who has himself acted as a 'conman' (the reader's term) - via the financial self-dealing, pardon practices, and accountability-evasion documented throughout this document - creates a broader cultural permission structure, in which other officials, companies, and individuals become more willing to act as though they too will not face consequences, whether or not any specific actor is consciously imitating Trump. What supports this read: the pardon-power entry (Bowman's 'permission structure' argument), the Jake Lang case, and the density of self-dealing across unrelated domains (media settlements, tariff exemptions, defense contracts, redistricting). What this thesis cannot claim honestly: that any specific unrelated actor changed behavior because of Trump's conduct specifically, as opposed to preexisting incentives predating this administration.
title: Reader's working thesis (not a sourced finding)
